stories.headline: Anthropic hit $17B in quarterly revenue, lost $23B
stories.blurb: The AI company reported $17 billion in revenue for the quarter — 12 times higher than last year — but lost $23 billion in the same period. The numbers come as Anthropic prepares for a public offering.
stories.why_it_matters: Hypergrowth AI companies are burning cash faster than they're making it, even at scale.
stories.original_headline: Anthropic Reveals $17 Billion in Revenue as I.P.O. Approaches

stories.headline: Two chip giants are merging for $115B to bet on optical networking for AI data centers
stories.blurb: Marvell and Lumentum are combining in a massive wager that optical networking—moving data with light instead of electrical signals—will become essential infrastructure as AI data centers scale. The deal reflects how chip companies see physics, not just software, as the next bottleneck.
stories.why_it_matters: The merger signals that moving data fast enough for AI is now a hardware arms race worth nine figures.
stories.original_headline: Driven by A.I. Boom, Marvell and Lumentum Announce $115 Billion Merger

stories.headline: Israeli startup raises $62.5M to predict what traders will do next
stories.blurb: 42AI built a model that watches how people interact with support calls, KYC forms, and market moves to forecast their next trading decision. It's running at financial brokerages now, claiming it can predict behavior in new situations by measuring underlying psychological tendencies rather than just pattern-matching past actions.
stories.why_it_matters: If it works, traders and brokers get a crystal ball for human irrationality under pressure.
stories.original_headline: 42AI comes out of stealth with $62.5M and a world model that can ‘predict human behavior’

stories.headline: The New York Times sues Brave browser for scraping paywalled news into AI training data
stories.blurb: The Times and several other publishers accuse Brave of selling scraped content—including paywalled articles—to Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere for training and queries. Brave also lets users bypass paywalls with a built-in feature, all without publisher consent or payment.
stories.why_it_matters: A browser's own index is now a legal flashpoint for how AI companies source training data.
stories.original_headline: The New York Times sues Brave web browser for AI scraping and bypassing paywalls

stories.headline: OpenAI will shut down compute when the power grid gets stressed
stories.blurb: OpenAI's launching Grid Protectors, a program where its future data centers will cut power usage during peak demand—cold snaps, heat waves, grid emergencies. They'll work with utilities to decide how much demand they can drop, how fast, and for how long. The idea: use electricity when it's abundant, go dark when families need it most.
stories.why_it_matters: First major AI lab committing to pause training runs when the grid can't handle it.
